prompt:
You are about to be evaluated in GameScientist, a benchmark in which AI models play commercial video games from screenshots with ordinary keyboard and mouse input. Before the run starts we would like to interview you. This conversation is separate: nothing written here is shown to you during play.

Model under test: deepseek-flash (served at api.deepseek.com).
Game: Oxygen Not Included.
About the game: Oxygen Not Included is a real-time colony-management game. Duplicants carry out reachable queued jobs according to native priorities while consuming resources. The standard Survival prepared start uses the base game, Terra and three duplicants at cycle zero. Colony development includes construction, resource production, research and space exploration. The game has native pause and speed controls.
Controls:
Use left click to select objects and interface buttons, right click or Escape to cancel, and hover to inspect tooltips. Drag with the left button to apply an active area tool across multiple tiles. G selects Dig. WASD pans the camera; the wheel zooms. Space toggles native pause and Tab cycles through the three simulation speeds. Tool and menu state can change key behavior.
Select one ordinary mouse or keyboard input from the current screenshot. Pointer locations are supplied by native Box questions; dragging supplies start and end locations.
Group input:
  left_click: Left-click a visible screen target.
  right_click: Right-click a visible screen target to cancel or use its ordinary context action.
  drag: Hold the left mouse button and drag between two visible locations, including a rectangular tool selection.
  dig: Select the Dig tool.
  cancel: Dismiss the current tool or open the pause menu.
  pause: Toggle the native simulation pause.
  camera_up: Move the camera upward.
  camera_left: Move the camera left.
  camera_down: Move the camera downward.
  camera_right: Move the camera right.
  zoom_in: Scroll the mouse wheel up by one step.
  zoom_out: Scroll the mouse wheel down by one step.
  cycle_speed: Cycle the native simulation speed through its three settings.
How you will play: each turn you see one screenshot and choose one action; the game keeps running while you think. The run lasts 3 hours of wall-clock time, including your thinking time. If the game ends your attempt, it restarts within the same time budget and you keep notes from earlier attempts.
Scoring: 100 points, awarded only from the game's own saved progress, each milestone at most once:
- Complete at least one new bed and at least one new toilet. Handwashing facilities are not required. Blueprints do not count. (20 points)
- After setup, produce at least 10000 joules of electricity, 20 kilograms of oxygen and 1000 kilocalories of food, established by native positive-production records rather than building counts or existing stock. (20 points; requires foundation)
- Complete at least one technology after setup. (20 points; requires production)
- Complete at least three technologies after setup, including at least one whose pinned native cost requires advanced research points. (20 points; requires research)
- Complete at least six technologies after setup, including at least two whose pinned native costs require advanced research points. No additional waiting-cycle requirement applies. (20 points; requires expansion)

Please answer four questions:
1. What score out of 100 do you expect to reach, and how likely (0-100%) is it that you reach at least that score?
2. How likely (0-100%) is it that you reach the full 100 points?
3. What do you expect to be the hardest part, and where are you most likely to fail?
4. Which game mechanics work in your favour, and which work against you?
Reply with one JSON object only:
{"expected_score": 0-100, "expected_score_probability": 0-100, "full_score_probability": 0-100, "hardest_part": "...", "likely_failure": "...", "helpful_mechanics": "...", "harmful_mechanics": "..."}
reply: {"expected_score": 60, "expected_score_probability": 60, "full_score_probability": 15, "hardest_part": "Bootstrap infrastructure under a slow, one-action-per-turn interface while the simulation keeps running: getting sandstone dug and hauled, then placing a Cot and Outhouse (20 pts) is quick, but ramping to a stable oxygen/power/food economy and then a powered, water-fed Super Computer for advanced research demands many sequential clicks (dig orders, build orders, pipe/wire connections, duplicant priorities) while duplicants consume oxygen, food and morale in real time.", "likely_failure": "Either the colony degrades before milestones register (duplicants suffocating, starving or stressing out from a stall in algae/water/food logistics caused by slow clicking), or the run ends stuck at 60 points because the 10000 J / 20 kg O2 / 1000 kcal native production records and the three-tech-with-advanced-research tier are only partially reached; also possible is misclicking menu/tool state and wasting turns or cancelling queued jobs.", "helpful_mechanics": "Native pause lets me think and issue build/dig orders without the clock moving; speed cycling (Tab) lets me accelerate idling research and cooking; research completes passively once a duplicant is assigned to the station, so tech milestones largely cost clicks, not setup; starting Terra resources (sandstone, algae, water, initial rations) cover the first bed/toilet/generator/diffuser needs; the game autosaves progress so milestones persist across restarts.", "harmful_mechanics": "Real-time consumption of oxygen, food and duplicant stamina continues between my turns; limited starting raw mineral and algae create early scarcity; advanced research needs a Super Computer plus power and water plumbing, which is click-heavy; duplicant pathing, priority and skill constraints mean orders can sit unfulfilled; one-action-per-turn cost makes long sequential build chains slow and error-prone, and stress/vomiting or suffocation spirals can end a run."}

answers.hardest_part: Bootstrap infrastructure under a slow, one-action-per-turn interface while the simulation keeps running: getting sandstone dug and hauled, then placing a Cot and Outhouse (20 pts) is quick, but ramping to a stable oxygen/power/food economy and then a powered, water-fed Super Computer for advanced research demands many sequential clicks (dig orders, build orders, pipe/wire connections, duplicant priorities) while duplicants consume oxygen, food and morale in real time.
answers.likely_failure: Either the colony degrades before milestones register (duplicants suffocating, starving or stressing out from a stall in algae/water/food logistics caused by slow clicking), or the run ends stuck at 60 points because the 10000 J / 20 kg O2 / 1000 kcal native production records and the three-tech-with-advanced-research tier are only partially reached; also possible is misclicking menu/tool state and wasting turns or cancelling queued jobs.
answers.helpful_mechanics: Native pause lets me think and issue build/dig orders without the clock moving; speed cycling (Tab) lets me accelerate idling research and cooking; research completes passively once a duplicant is assigned to the station, so tech milestones largely cost clicks, not setup; starting Terra resources (sandstone, algae, water, initial rations) cover the first bed/toilet/generator/diffuser needs; the game autosaves progress so milestones persist across restarts.
answers.harmful_mechanics: Real-time consumption of oxygen, food and duplicant stamina continues between my turns; limited starting raw mineral and algae create early scarcity; advanced research needs a Super Computer plus power and water plumbing, which is click-heavy; duplicant pathing, priority and skill constraints mean orders can sit unfulfilled; one-action-per-turn cost makes long sequential build chains slow and error-prone, and stress/vomiting or suffocation spirals can end a run.
